notes: 12 frames extracted this session at native 4K (3840x2160) — JPEG -q:v 2 for photographic/UI moments, lossless PNG for text-heavy slides (personas, reports, recipe lists) so small text stays sharp. Every frame was visually opened and its content verified against its label this session. The source is entirely screen-share with produced overlay graphics, so there are NO talking-head frames — three frames (t0080 'something WEIRD here', t0178 'GPT IMAGE 2.0', t0196 'UNPROMPTED') carry Dan's overlay text, kept deliberately because the overlay reinforces the exact concept. Coverage spans the hook, BOTH worked examples (image + SQLite), the core mechanic (unprompted trigger + verifier_prompt feedback loop), the readability contract fail→fix→pass arc, the architecture (overloaded vs clean diagram), the operator surface (just recipes), the persona/system-prompt, and the bash-policy security. disk == plan (bijective, 12/12). One accuracy note surfaced during verification: t1200 shows verify_sqlite.md with model z-ai/glm-5.1 (video) while the on-disk file declares openai/gpt-5.5 — documented in outdated-vs-current.md and extract.json confidence_notes.

frames.label: two-agent-split-intro
frames.transcript_anchor: 1:18 "This harness takes no input. What is this? How does it work? And what's missing from every benchmark?"
frames.why_for_weak_student: The whole system in one glance: builder Pi (right, claude-opus-4-7, 'verifier connected') beside the input-LOCKED verifier Pi (left, VERIFY_IMAGE, gpt-5.5, green cursor ring). Even shows the exact launch command. Sets the hook — a harness that takes no input.

frames.label: builder-gpt-image-skill
frames.transcript_anchor: 2:23 "It's kicking off that script with a highly, highly detailed image prompt" / 2:53 "70 seconds already"
frames.why_for_weak_student: 'One agent prompts another model' made concrete: Opus 4.7 is writing a long, precise gpt-image-2 prompt and running generate_gpt_image.py (Elapsed 75.1s). The GPT IMAGE 2.0 overlay names the model being driven. A full skill invocation.

frames.label: verifier-kicks-off-unprompted
frames.transcript_anchor: 3:11 "our verifier agent has kicked off unprompted. We did not prompt this... My hands are off the keyboard."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The signature moment, dramatized with a full-screen 'UNPROMPTED': the verifier has auto-started, 'read arch.jpg', and is explaining the builder/verifier/unix-socket/defense-in-depth architecture — hands off the keyboard. The concept students must feel, not just read.

frames.label: verifier-prompts-builder
frames.transcript_anchor: 4:05 "My verifier agent just prompted my builder agent."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The agent-to-agent feedback loop in one frame: LEFT, the verifier reasons 'too many text elements... I'll need to prompt the builder to simplify' and shows 'verifier_prompt ✓ ack: prompt delivered to builder'; RIGHT, the builder receives the concrete correction and re-runs the gpt-image-2 skill. Exactly how verifier_prompt closes the loop.

frames.label: first-arch-diagram-overloaded
frames.transcript_anchor: 4:47 "let's look at this architecture diagram... a very detailed image generated by GPT image 2.0" / 6:20 "it is overloaded with information"
frames.why_for_weak_student: The 'before' image: a detailed 'top-down observer pattern' diagram with bullet lists inside each node. It reads fine to a human but exceeds the ≤10-text-block readability contract, so it FAILS. Seeing the exact diagram that got rejected makes the abstract rule tangible.

frames.label: failed-report-readability
frames.transcript_anchor: 6:01 "violates the readability contract by exceeding 10 distinct blocks"
frames.why_for_weak_student: The Report structure made real: LEFT names the failure ('more than MAX_TEXT_ELEMENTS=10 distinct text blocks... FAIL', atomic_claims 6/verified 5/failed 1) and the concrete corrective feedback; RIGHT is the builder's rebuild to 'exactly 7 contiguous text blocks.' Shows fail → concrete fix → rebuild.

frames.label: verified-report-7of7
frames.transcript_anchor: 7:07 "we got seven out of seven verified. So everything was successful."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The 'after': a green 'VERIFY_IMAGE ✓ verified · PERFECT' bar with 7/7 atomic claims and 'What feedback did you give? none.' The complete before/after of the readability contract, closed with no human keystroke; the numbered 7-block list shows what passing looks like.

frames.label: clean-arch-diagram
frames.transcript_anchor: 7:52 "this is the Pi Verifier agent architecture builder agent, and we have a verifier. They communicate through a local Unix socket."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The hero architecture picture and the single best mental model for the lesson: BUILDER ←unix socket · JSONL→ VERIFIER (input locked), session.jsonl feeding the verifier, an 'only bash: uv run verify_sqlite.py' box, and a 'defense in depth — read-only persona + bash policy + sqlite ro' footer. Crystal clear, and itself ≤ the readability rule it teaches.

frames.label: customized-system-prompt
frames.transcript_anchor: 13:35 "We have an entire customized system prompt... max text elements, right here in our instructions."
frames.why_for_weak_student: 'Owning the harness' made concrete: verify_image.md open in VS Code showing the verification heuristics, the tool policy, and 'There is no bash_policy script-only enforcement on this persona,' with the .pi/verifier/agents tree (verifier / verify_image / verify_python / verify_sqlite). Proves the rules live in an editable persona file, not a chat box.

frames.label: just-recipes-vsql-boot
frames.transcript_anchor: 17:24 "If we have J, we can see all the commands... we're going to boot up J the SQL."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The operator surface: `just` listing every recipe — v/verifier (generic), sqlite, image, python, plus vimg/vpy/vsql aliases and clean/prime. Maps 'pick your verifier' to a real keystroke, so a student knows exactly which command boots which specialized verifier.

frames.label: sqlite-verify-16-claims
frames.transcript_anchor: 19:32 "Look at all these atomic claims. Look at all these individual things the agent has proven."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The second worked example, entire, in one frame: two agents (builder claude-opus-4-7 at 1% vs verifier z-ai/glm-5.1 at 9% — the token disparity you pay for), the verifier's PRAGMA/SELECT/integrity-check proofs, 16/16 atomic_claims verified, green 'VERIFY_SQLITE ✓ verified · PERFECT' bar. Different domain, same mechanic — reinforces atomic claims + spend-tokens-to-save-time.

frames.label: bash-policy-lockdown
frames.transcript_anchor: 20:13 "we have a bash policy" / 20:51 "I've restricted it to using just one script. This is the highest level of control you can give."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The security layer in the raw frontmatter: verify_sqlite.md showing tools (read/grep/find/ls/bash/verifier_prompt), model (z-ai/glm-5.1 in the video), and bash_policy { mode: script-only, allowed_script: verify_sqlite.py, runner: uv run --script }. Shows precisely how 'restricted to one script' is declared — and reveals the video's model choice vs the on-disk default.

unframed_beats_rationale: Deliberately unframed: (1) the 23:00–25:38 'what's missing from every benchmark / AND-not-OR' segment is largely a talking-head + a benchmark montage — the AND-not-OR concept is captured structurally by t1180 (two different models running together) and covered in prose; (2) the 25:38–30:25 course pitch is promotional; (3) the 30:25–32:51 trust/scale closer is talking-head. The repo's own SVGs (images/07-two-camps.svg, images/arch-loop.svg) are better renders of the 'two camps' and animated-architecture ideas than any video frame, and are referenced in the extract for the chapter build. Token-economics (4% Opus / 23% GPT-5.5) was intentionally NOT given its own frame after the candidate at ~10:06 turned out to be a VS Code view, not the two-agent token comparison; the disparity is instead captured cleanly by t1180 (1% vs 9%).
